_note: SERP for 'tripod for wildlife photography' read via Firecrawl on 2026-10-20. Top 10 organic: 1 Gitzo maker article (read; maker content, not counted), 2 Sirui store collection (maker catalog, skipped), 3 Reddit r/AskPhotography thread (blocked for full text; only the search snippet seen, which names Leofoto Ranger Pro LS-284C), 4 Better With Birds guide (read; names no tripod models), 5 YouTube (skipped), 6 B&H category page (shop, skipped), 7 schultzphoto.com (read; buying advice only, no models named except an unnamed Manfrotto), 8 Facebook group post (login wall; snippet only, names Mefoto, K&F Concept, Leofoto), 9 BCG Forums thread (read in full; names Gitzo Systematic 3-series/Mountaineer, RRS, Leofoto LS324CX, Leofoto Ranger-225CEX), 10 Shutter Muse head guide (read; heads only, RRS TVC-34L Mk2 mentioned in passing). Only the Leofoto Ranger carbon line is named by 2+ countable pages (Reddit, BCG; Facebook snippet as a third), so productCount is lowered from 6 to 1. The pages name different Ranger models (Reddit LS-284C Pro, BCG LS-324CX and Ranger-225CEX); LS-284C is the 4-section member Reddit named and the one with the most owner write-ups, but this is a family match, not an identical-model match across pages. Maker page read: leofoto.net LS-284C kit (includes LH-30 ball head); B&H LS-284CX page read for the variant with the improved latch. IMPORTANT FIT CAVEAT: this is a travel-class tripod, 47 in without column; an owner on Fred Miranda called it too short for telephoto use unless the photographer is short, so it suits 100-400/150-600 class zooms, not 500-600mm primes.

products.name: Leofoto LS-284C Ranger
products.query: Leofoto LS-284C Ranger carbon fiber tripod
products.badge: Best lightweight carbon pick for telephoto zooms
products.summary: A 4-section, 28 mm carbon fiber tripod rated for 10 kg (22 lb) that weighs about 2.4 lb as bare legs and folds to roughly 18-19 in. It is the Leofoto Ranger model most often named in wildlife and landscape threads, and it holds 100-400mm class telephoto zooms well, but its 47 in height without the column is short for long-lens work.
products.renterNote: Hikers and bird or wildlife shooters carrying a mirrorless or DSLR body with a 100-400mm or 150-600mm zoom who want a light carbon tripod; the key caveat is height (about 47 in without the screw-in column, so tall shooters raise the column) and that supertelephoto primes like a 600mm f/4 need a larger Leofoto series or a gimbal-capable tripod.
pros: 10 kg (22 lb) rated load on 10-layer carbon fiber legs with a bare-legs weight near 2.4 lb
Folds to about 18-19 in and the leg angles lock at 23, 55 and 85 degrees for low ground-level shots
Screw-in center column is optional, so you can leave it at home or add height when needed
cons: Height is about 47 in without the column (about 60 in with it), which owners find short for long telephoto lenses
Twist leg locks are not sealed against dust or water, and the lower leg sections can flex under hand pressure
facts: Maker (Leofoto kit page): LS-284C Ranger, load 10 kg, max working height 1,270 mm without ball head and center column, max height 128 cm, carrying length 53 cm, twist locks, rubber foot/spike combination, weight 1.43 kg with LH-30 ball head
B&H lists the LS-284CX variant at 22 lb / 10 kg, 3.1 to 65 in working height, 19 in closed, 2.4 lb, 4 sections, 23/55/85 degree leg angles, twist locks
Lonely Speck: 50 in with ball head and legs fully extended, 60.4 in with the center column, LH-30 ball head rated 33 lb by Leofoto

specs.Weight: About 2.4 lb (1.1 kg) legs only; 1.43 kg (3.1 lb) with LH-30 ball head per maker and Lonely Speck
specs.Material: 10-layer carbon fiber legs, CNC 6061-T6 aluminum parts
specs.Max height (column raised): About 60 in (maker/owner figures; B&H lists the CX at 64.6 in)
specs.Max height (column down): About 47 in (127 mm is the maker's 1,270 mm; about 50 in with ball head)
specs.Min height: About 2.75 in at the 85 degree leg angle (Fred Miranda owner)
specs.Folded length: About 18.7 in (B&H, CX); 53 cm carrying length with head (maker)
specs.Head: Kit version includes LH-30 ball head (15 kg per maker); legs-only versions exist
specs.Plate: Arca-Swiss compatible on the LH-30 head

products.scoreNote: Stability 7: owners found a 400mm zoom steady, but the legs flex when pressed and long primes want a bigger tripod. Portability 9: about 2.4 lb legs and under 20 in folded. Height 5: 47 in without the column is short for telephoto work. Build 8: 10-layer carbon, CNC aluminum, replaceable feet, but unsealed locks. Value 9: carbon at a mid-range price with spikes, case and column included.

praise: Stiff and steady with 100-400mm class zooms and a heavy 105mm prime, with vibration settling in a couple of seconds
Very small folded size and light enough to strap to a pack or carry-on
Smooth leg extension, secure twist locks and a quick-attach center column that owners found stable
complaints: Too short without the center column for taller shooters or long telephoto setups
Lower leg sections flex when pressed hard, and twist locks are not sealed against dust or water
